key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

raw.rationale: The presence of numerous eosinophils in the biopsy and the clinical presentation of erythematous annular plaques without scale are consistent with Eosinophilic annular erythema (EAE), which is also known to be associated with immunotherapy.

rejected.label: Wells syndrome
rejected.why: While Wells syndrome also presents with eosinophilia, it typically has a more acute onset and is associated with flame figures on histology, which were not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: This condition can present similarly but does not typically have the significant eosinophilic infiltration seen in this patient's biopsy.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Granuloma annulare is characterized by granulomatous inflammation, which was not described in the biopsy findings of this patient.
